description: Minimal RQ (Redis Queue) project with enqueue producers and a Worker consumer. Gates the two ENQUEUES edges that carry the RQ producer hop — notify_user -> send_email from queue.enqueue(callable), and request_report -> generate_report from queue.enqueue_call(func="workers.email.generate_report"), where the target is a dotted STRING and still resolves — plus the CALLS / CONTAINS / IMPORTS shape. RQ emits no PRODUCES and never CONSUMES, and that is deliberate: #6741 arm 4 found rq.go's producer regexes scan the SAME call sites synthesizeRQEnqueueEdges already covers, so a PRODUCES edge would be the double pair ADR-0028 §3 forbids; queue-style dispatch onto a FUNCTION takes ENQUEUES, while the scheduler-style dispatch onto a job CLASS in Java Quartz and C# Hangfire/Quartz.NET takes PRODUCES. The Worker CONSUMES row below stays nice_to_have and is UNMET: nothing in the tree emits CONSUMES in any language (known gap, recorded in ADR-0028), so the Worker entity carries only the structural CONTAINS edge from its file and reaches no job it consumes.

expected_relationships.note: #6490 arm B, and the single most load-bearing edge in this fixture: `notification_queue.enqueue(send_email, …)` binds the producer to the consumer function in another file. RQ is the only queue framework in the corpus that emits ENQUEUES — see the FINDING on python-dramatiq-mini.

`report_queue.enqueue_call(func="workers.email.generate_report", args=[report_id])` — the target is a dotted STRING, not a symbol, and it still resolves to the real function. That string-resolution path is what this row protects.
The enqueue call site itself, distinct from the ENQUEUES edge it produces.
`def notify_user(user_id: int, message: str) -> None:` at module level.
`from workers.email import send_email, generate_report` — resolves across files to the real definitions.
`from rq import Queue, Worker` — only worker_runner.py imports Worker, so this row also pins that the two files' import sets are not merged.

#6490 arm B FINDING: the Worker entity this fixture asserts as a must-have has ZERO edges. `Worker([notification_queue, report_queue], connection=redis_conn)` names the two queues it drains — the same two `Queue("notifications")` / `Queue("reports")` objects that api/notifications.py enqueues onto — and nothing in the graph connects the worker to either queue or to any consumer function. The producer half of this fixture is modelled and the consumer half is an island, which is precisely what a fixture asserting zero relationships could never report.

#6490 arm B FINDING: the queue NAME is nowhere in the graph. `Queue("notifications", connection=redis_conn)` and `Queue("reports", …)` produce no message_topic or queue entity, so the ENQUEUES edges above jump producer→consumer directly and the routing key that decides which worker picks the job up is lost.
